claims.text: The baseline Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy has minimal short-range chemical order and a relatively low density of nanoscale precipitates.
Slight changes in Al content combined with annealing increase short-range chemical ordering in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Increased short-range ordering promotes formation of L12-like γ′ precipitates.
The resulting L12-like γ′ precipitates are coherent and nanoscale.
Formation of L12-like precipitates stabilizes a single-phase microstructure.
Increasing or reducing Al content modulates local chemical potential and thereby enhances or impedes short-range ordering.
Enhanced short-range ordering reduces free-energy fluctuations.
Enhanced ordering restricts atomic mobility and suppresses unwanted phase transformations.
At lower temperatures, favorable ordering enthalpy in high-entropy alloys can overcome configurational entropy and affect phase stability.
L12 γ′ precipitation can improve thermal stability, coarsening resistance, and high-temperature strength retention.
The proposed ordered precipitates strengthen the alloy by acting as barriers to dislocation motion.
Optimized short-range order and precipitate density improve radiation tolerance by reducing the number and size of irradiation-induced defects.
Optimized short-range order and L12-like precipitation improve or preserve oxidation resistance and environmental durability.
Optimized short-range order and L12-like precipitation maintain or improve cryogenic toughness.
Optimized alloy variants will have a higher and more uniform density of coherent nanoscale precipitates than the baseline.
Annealing from 873 K to 1073 K promotes controlled nanoscale ordering in this alloy system.
An inert annealing atmosphere prevents oxidation while ordering develops.
A statistically significant correlation between measured ordering or precipitate density and the targeted performance metrics is required by the proposed hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis calls the stabilized microstructure single-phase while also requiring a distinct L12-like γ′ precipitate phase within a matrix; a matrix-plus-precipitate microstructure is ordinarily multiphase unless 'single-phase' is redefined.

The central claim concerns an optimized degree of ordering, but the falsification rule says that degradation caused by excessive or insufficient ordering would falsify it. Such degradation is compatible with an optimum and therefore is not, by itself, contradictory evidence.
